newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Frenchman's August Mir flight scrapped - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Frenchman's August Mir flight scrapped - Interfax.

text.p: Frenchman Leopold Eyharts will not be part of a relief crew due to replace the three cosmonauts on board the troubled Mir space station in August, Interfax news agency quoted Russian space officials as saying on Monday.

It said a meeting of senior space officials and designers decided to send only two Russians, Anatoly Solovyov and Pavel Vinogradov, to Mir, where they will have to undertake risky repair works. Additional equipment will be sent up in the Soyuz spacecraft instead of Eyharts, it said.
The meeting is taking place at Russia's Energiya company, a space rocket producer, near Mission Control at Korolyov outside Moscow.
Vinogradov and Solovyov are due to blast off for Mir on August 5 and should reach the space station on August 7.

A cargo craft hit Mir during a training docking on June 25 and holed a module attached to the station, damaging the power supply. The crew have suffered a series of mishaps since then, including a computer crash caused by human error last week.

Space officials have made clear they think Mir's crew -- Russians Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin and British-born NASA physicist Michael Foale -- should not do the repairs. A final announcement on who carries out the repairs is expected later on Monday.
